source.title: Video context-dependent effects in recognition memory

confidence_rationale: Corroborates the boundary side of MECH-339: it shows the context channel carries real, recoverable retrieval signal (a richer dynamic context reinstates context-dependent recognition where static photographic contexts often produce null effects), which is what justifies including a context channel at all. But it is mixed for the claim because it primarily varies context salience rather than the item-cue strength that defines the outshining gate; it bounds and motivates the context channel without testing the gate's conditional shape directly. Held at 0.50 to reflect that indirectness plus abstract-level assessment.
failure_signatures: Static, low-information contexts can yield null context-dependent recognition even when an episode was encoded there -- so a context channel whose salience term is flat (insensitive to how much contextual information is actually available) would over-credit weak contexts and predict effects the data do not show.

Context-dependent recognition is fragile and depends on context richness; a model that treats any stored SD-039 payload as an equally strong context cue regardless of its informational content would mispredict the conditions under which the fallback actually helps.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Dynamic video contexts produce reliable environmental context-dependent recognition effects, in contrast to the weak and often null effects obtained with static photographic contexts. Richer, more distinctive contextual information at encoding and test yields a stronger contextual retrieval cue and a measurable context-dependent recognition advantage.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the existence and gradedness of MECH-339's context channel: there is a real, recoverable contextual retrieval signal whose strength scales with the informational content of the stored context, which is the premise behind composing a context channel from the SD-039 payload (arousal_tag/last_vs/cause) and weighting it by a context-salience term (context_salience = 1 - exp(-arousal_tag/arousal_scale)). It also bounds the channel: contexts that are informationally thin contribute little, so the salience term must be sensitive to how much context is actually stored, not flat.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper varies CONTEXT richness (video vs photo), not the direct item-cue strength that defines the outshining gate, so it speaks to the magnitude and reality of the context channel rather than to the gating rule itself. The 'richness' manipulation is a loose analogue of MECH-339's context_salience, not a direct test of the arousal_tag composition; and as with the 2018 paper the substrate is human verbal recognition, not goal-bank retrieval.
mapping.source_context: Human behavioural recognition-memory experiments contrasting dynamic (video) vs static (photographic) environmental contexts; same Shizuoka University programme.

confidence_components.notes: Strong venue and careful design (high source quality). Mapping fidelity moderate: it validates that a context channel carries graded, real retrieval signal (the premise for including one and for a salience weight) but does not test the outshining gate's conditional shape -- that is why it is logged 'mixed' rather than 'supports'. Transfer risk moderate for the same human->agent reasons as the companion 2018 entry.
